Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with our legal redlines for the Master Agreement and SLA. We attached a short SLA redline that includes two items that are blocking approval on our side:

1) Termination & cure: the ability to terminate for repeated critical (P1) availability/latency breaches.
2) Financial remedy: a liquidated damages construct (not just service credits) for repeat, sustained P1 outages — our standard is a per-breach fee equal to 25% of monthly recurring fees, cumulative and subject to a cap.

Our security/compliance and finance teams need a deterministic remedy (contractual cash) in addition to credits — credits have proven insufficient for customer-facing outages. I know many vendors push back on LDs, but procurement will need either a capped liquidated damages clause or an explicit fee-at-risk + termination pathway to move forward.

I've attached SLA_Redline_HealthAtlas_v1.pdf and a simple MA cost model (HealthAtlas_MA-Proposal.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to discuss a capped LD or a fee-at-risk escrow? If not, what equivalent compromise would you consider?

Proposed next step: 30-minute call this week with legal and procurement. Availability: Thu morning PT or Fri midday PT.

Thanks,

Alex — thanks for the redline and the clear ask. We appreciate the urgency. Quick summary of where we stand:

- Redwood's standard position: we offer structured service credits tied to SLOs, escalation paths, and termination rights in very narrow circumstances. We almost always avoid traditional "liquidated damages" language because it creates open-ended liability and procurement exposures that are difficult to underwrite.

- That said, we can be flexible for enterprise customers on larger, strategic deals. Two options we typically propose as compromises:
  1) Fee-at-risk (escrowed) model: customer-funded escrow equal to N months of recurring fees that is released against validated breaches according to a defined schedule, with a capped total payout.
  2) Limited termination rights: explicit, staged termination after repeated, uncured P1 incidents (with defined cure windows and a cap on total payout), plus the option for a capped buyout in lieu of punitive LDs.

Before a call, can you confirm (a) target MRR for the initial 12 months (so we can size any escrow), and (b) whether Procurement requires a statutory "liquidated damages" clause or simply certainty of cash remedies (we can express this as an escrow/buyout in our documents).

I'm looping in Ben Carter (AE) to align commercial context. If these framing options look reasonable, we can get legal to draft a short compromise term sheet for HealthAtlas. Thu morning PT works for a 30-min slot if you still have availability.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Alex — thanks for the clarity and for looping in Elena. We understand the need for deterministic cash remedies for HealthAtlas' procurement and finance teams. Redwood's legal and commercial teams reviewed your redline and we've worked up a short, pragmatic counterproposal we believe meets procurement's objectives while protecting Redwood from open-ended liability. Summary below; I've attached a one-page commercial term sheet we can walk through on a call.

Redwood counterproposal (two options — pick one):

Option A — Escrowed fee-at-risk + staged termination
- Escrow amount: pre-funded by HealthAtlas equal to 3 months of contracted net recurring fees (calculated on initial 12-month ARR).
- Automatic release schedule: for each validated P1 (per the SLA's incident validation process), 25% of the escrow is released to HealthAtlas (no-fault release once incident is validated).
- Cure & remediation: Redwood has 30 days from discovery to cure each incident; incidents not cured become eligible for payout.
- Staged termination: HealthAtlas may elect to terminate if 3 validated P1s occur in a rolling 90-day window and Redwood fails to cure as set out above.
- Total cap: total payouts from escrow capped at 6 months of MRR; any remaining escrow after exhaustion is returned to HealthAtlas.

Option B — Limited buyout (single cash remedy + termination option)
- Buyout amount: one-time cash payment equal to 3 months of contracted net recurring fees, payable to HealthAtlas if customer elects termination following 2 validated P1s in a rolling 60-day window and failure to cure within a 30-day remediation period.
- This option is more restrictive: it provides a defined cash remedy and a clear termination path, but there are no ongoing per-breach payouts beyond the one-time buyout.

Additional notes:
- We will use our incident validation process (postmortem + severity classification by CS and product) to determine whether a P1 is validated; Monica will be the CS point of contact for incident verification.
- These options replace a traditional liquidated damages clause; Redwood will not accept uncapped LD language.
- We are open to a short, objective escalation SLA and an executive remediation playbook as conditions precedent.

Next steps: if either option is acceptable in principle, we will: (1) circulate a 1-page term sheet and redline to the SLA showing the proposed escrow/buyout language, (2) set a 30–45 minute call with legal and procurement to finalize sizing and mechanics. Thanks — we want to get this across the finish line.
